title: Russia commissions Yasen-M nuclear submarine Perm, which Moscow says carries Zircon hypersonic missiles
summary: President Vladimir Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony at the Sevmash shipyard in Severodvinsk on 27 November marking the formal transfer of the Project 885M Yasen-M nuclear-powered submarine Perm to the Russian navy. Moscow says the Perm is the first submarine equipped with Zircon hypersonic missiles. Putin said the navy would receive five more submarines by 2030, three of them Yasen-M class.

reported_claims.text: The Yasen-M class nuclear-powered submarine Perm was formally transferred to the navy at a flag-raising ceremony attended by Putin at the Sevmash shipyard in Severodvinsk on Friday 27 November.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Kremlin video, as reported by AFP

reported_claims.text: The Perm is the first submarine equipped with Russia's Zircon hypersonic missiles.
The navy will receive five more submarines by 2030, including three Yasen-M class boats, able to operate in any part of the world's oceans with a range of cruise missiles.

unknowns: Independent confirmation that Zircon is integrated and operational on the Perm
Whether the two cited reports draw on the same AFP copy
reassessment_triggers: First reported Zircon test launch from the Perm
Deployment of the Perm near NATO or US waters
impact_assessment: Potential: incremental growth in Russia's long-range submarine strike capability and in the hypersonic threat to naval and coastal targets.
priority_rationale: LOW: a planned capability milestone with no immediate operational event.
monitoring_actions: Track Russian navy announcements on Zircon tests and Perm deployment

sources.title: Putin unveils new Russian nuclear-powered submarine with hypersonic weapons
